instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `ep_sqrt_range`. ep_sqrt must be a square root across the whole f64 range, not only near 1. It used to run ten Heron steps from y = x. Heron converges quadratically only once the iterate is near the root; from y = x it first needs ~log2(sqrt(x)). It should compile and run successfully.
description: ep_sqrt must be a square root across the whole f64 range, not only near 1. It used to run ten Heron steps from y = x. Heron converges quadratically only once the iterate is near the root; from y = x it first needs ~log2(sqrt(x))
comments: ep_sqrt must be a square root across the whole f64 range, not only near 1.
It used to run ten Heron steps from y = x. Heron converges quadratically only
once the iterate is near the root; from y = x it first needs ~log2(sqrt(x))
halving steps just to get close, so a fixed step count silently bounds the
range over which the result is a square root at all.
Measured 2026-09-09 before the fix, as relative residual |y*y - x| / x:
Accurate only for x in about [1e-4, 1e4] and catastrophically wrong outside,
which reached ep_std, ep_sqrt_ep, ep_rel_uncertainty and ep_budget -- all of
them thin wrappers over ep_sqrt(variance). A variance of 1e-6, an ordinary
measurement uncertainty, made ep_std report a standard deviation 29.6% off.
The oracle here is the residual, not a table of expected digits: y is a
square root of x exactly when y*y == x to within rounding, and that is
checkable without an external sqrt (ADR-008 keeps the oracle in Sounio).
Tolerance is 1e-12 relative. After the fix the measured residual is at most
~1 ulp (2.2e-16) at every point below -- exactly 0 only where x is a perfect
square in f64 -- so the bound leaves ~4 orders of magnitude of slack while
still being ~7e11 times tighter than the old behaviour at 1e6.
It is deliberately NOT an equality check. y*y == x holds for 1, 4, 1e6 and
the other f64-representable squares, and fails for 2 (residual 2.2e-16), 3
and 1e-6. A first draft of this file's notes claimed a residual of 0
everywhere; that was truncation in the measurement, not exactness, and the
mandatory math-review offload caught it.

Lowerer's locals stack, REUSED across function bodies at compile time:
`count` resets to 0 when lowering moves to the next function, but the
backing arrays are not cleared. The normal `bind_local` path zeroes

lower_fn_params_ref -- did not, so a tuple-array local's mask bit could
survive into a later, unrelated function's slot at the same table row.
`poison`'s only local (`t`, table row 0) is a tuple whose slot 0 is an
`[f64; 2]` array, setting row 0's mask bit 0. `victim`'s PARAMETER `t`
(also row 0, since each function's locals start over at row 0) is a
DIFFERENT tuple whose slot 0 is `[i64; 2]`, not a float array at all.
Before the direct parameter binder populated (and reset) its own mask,
row 0's stale bit 0 = 1 survived, so `victim`'s `t.0` read as an f64
array and corrupted the plain i64 elements.

Deep-research (peer-reviewed: Gresnigt et al., EPJC 2019 s10052-019-6967-1 / 2024 s10052-024-13476-0;
arXiv 2306.13098) establishes: the left-multiplication algebra of the complexified sedenions ℂ⊗𝕊 is
the Clifford algebra Cℓ(8) ≅ ℂ(16) (256 = 2^8 maps), the rank-4 step up from the octonionic Cℓ(6)
(64 = 2^6) that underlies Furey's one-generation SM construction. This test certifies the Clifford
PRESENTATION exactly: the eight left-multiplication operators L_1..L_8 pairwise anticommute and each
squares to −I — eight anticommuting √(−I) generators = a Cℓ(8) presentation. The 8th generator is
L_8 = e_8, the octonion→sedenion doubling unit (so e_8 is exactly the extra Clifford generator).
Uses the SPARSE identity: e_i·e_k = σ(i,k)·e_{i⊕k}, so L_i has one entry σ(i,k) per column k at row
i⊕k. Then (L_i L_j)[r][c] = σ(i,j⊕c)σ(j,c) at row r=i⊕j⊕c, giving:
{L_i,L_j}[i⊕j⊕c][c] = σ(i,j⊕c)σ(j,c) + σ(j,i⊕c)σ(i,c)   (anticommute ⟺ 0 ∀c)
(L_i²)[c][c] = σ(i,i⊕c)σ(i,c)                             (= −I ⟺ all −1)
No matrix multiplication needed. Also verified: 42 of the 105 pairs {L_i,L_j} do NOT anticommute
(the sedenion non-associativity signature), and ALL 42 are lower-upper (touch the doubling half);
the maximal mutually-anticommuting set has 8 generators ⟹ ladder rank 4; and the Gresnigt
S3-invariant charge Q_1 = (N_1+N_2+N_3 − 3 N_4)/3 on the 2^4 Fock space gives the SM electric-charge
multiset {0, ±1/3, ±2/3, ±1}. (The physical THREE-GENERATION interpretation of Cℓ(8)/S3 is a
modelling assumption, flagged OPEN — see docs/research/sedenion_clifford8.md.)
Decidable integer arithmetic, no float. SELF-CONTAINED. Cross-verified vs the operator's numpy
script and scripts/research/sedenion_clifford8_oracle.py by the gate + Lean.

// Build a main that loads f64 1.5 into rdi and calls print_f64, then exit(0)
fn emit_main(code: CodeBuffer, print_f64_off: i64) -> CodeBuffer with Mut {
    var c = code
    // mov rax, IEEE754(1.5) = 0x3FF8000000000000
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x48); c = emit_byte(c, 0xb8)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0xf8); c = emit_byte(c, 0x3f)
    // mov rdi, rax
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x48); c = emit_byte(c, 0x89); c = emit_byte(c, 0xc7)
    // call print_f64 (rel32)
    let call_site = c.len
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xe8)
    let rel = print_f64_off - (call_site + 5)
    c = emit_byte(c, rel & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 8) & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 16) & 0xFF)
    c = emit_byte(c, (rel >> 24) & 0xFF)
    // mov edi, 0 (exit code)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xbf); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    // mov eax, 60 (sys_exit)
    c = emit_byte(c, 0xb8); c = emit_byte(c, 0x3c); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00); c = emit_byte(c, 0x00)
    // syscall
    c = emit_byte(c, 0x0f); c = emit_byte(c, 0x05)
    c
}

    // Build code: print_f64 at offset 0, then main stub
    var code = code_buffer_new()
    code = ast_emit_print_f64_builtin(code)
    let main_off = code.len
    code = emit_main(code, 0)  // print_f64 is at code offset 0

    let code_size = code.len
    let vaddr_base: i64 = 0x400000
    let code_file_off: i64 = 0x80  // After ELF header (64 bytes) + 1 program header (56 bytes) = 120 = 0x78, round up
    let entry_vaddr = vaddr_base + code_file_off + main_off

    // Build minimal ELF64 header
    var elf: [i8; 4096] = [0; 4096]

    // ELF magic: 7f 45 4c 46
    elf[0 as usize] = 0x7f as i8
    elf[1 as usize] = 0x45 as i8  // E
    elf[2 as usize] = 0x4c as i8  // L
    elf[3 as usize] = 0x46 as i8  // F

    // EI_CLASS=2 (64-bit), EI_DATA=1 (LE), EI_VERSION=1, EI_OSABI=0
    elf[4 as usize] = 2 as i8
    elf[5 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[6 as usize] = 1 as i8
    elf[7 as usize] = 0 as i8

    // e_type=2 (ET_EXEC), e_machine=0x3E (x86-64)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 16, 2)
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 18, 0x3E)
    // e_version=1
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 20, 1)
    // e_entry
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 24, entry_vaddr)
    // e_phoff = 64 (right after ELF header)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 32, 64)
    // e_shoff = 0 (no section headers)
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 40, 0)
    // e_flags = 0
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 48, 0)
    // e_ehsize = 64
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 52, 64)
    // e_phentsize = 56
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 54, 56)
    // e_phnum = 1
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 56, 1)
    // e_shentsize = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 58, 0)
    // e_shnum = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 60, 0)
    // e_shstrndx = 0
    elf = emit_u16(elf, 62, 0)

    // Program header (LOAD) at offset 64
    // p_type = 1 (PT_LOAD)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 64, 1)
    // p_flags = 5 (PF_R | PF_X)
    elf = emit_u32(elf, 68, 5)
    // p_offset = 0
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 72, 0)
    // p_vaddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 80, vaddr_base)
    // p_paddr = vaddr_base
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 88, vaddr_base)
    // p_filesz = code_file_off + code_size
    let total_file = code_file_off + code_size
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 96, total_file)
    // p_memsz = total_file
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 104, total_file)
    // p_align = 0x1000
    elf = emit_u64(elf, 112, 0x1000)

    // Copy code bytes into ELF at code_file_off
    var ci: i64 = 0
    while ci < code_size {
        elf[(code_file_off + ci) as usize] = code.bytes[ci as usize]
        ci = ci + 1
    }

    let elf_size = code_file_off + code_size

    // Write ELF to file using VM builtin
    let wr = write_file("/tmp/sprint235_f64.elf", elf, elf_size)
    if wr < 0 {
        print("FAIL: could not write ELF\n")
        return 1
    }

    print("PASS: ELF written size=")
    print_int(elf_size)
    print(" entry=0x")
    print_int(entry_vaddr)
    print(" code=")
    print_int(code_size)
    print("\n")
    0
}
